messages:
jamie (support): heads-up — customer Acme CI pipelines started failing on our hosted API during nightly deploys around 2026-03-14 UTC. Error from their runners: 403 PermissionDenied, message: \"token missing required scope: inference.write\". they say the token is an ephemeral service-account token minted by our ci-helper with TTL=300s.

alex (sre): ok can you paste the curl/log they used? is it hitting the same region? TTL 300s is short if there's queueing.

jamie (support): pasted snippet from their job: ```curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer $CI_SA_TOKEN\" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-rt-1","input":"smoke test"}'``` response headers: ```HTTP/2 403 \ncontent-type: application/json\n x-request-id: rr-0a1b2c\n...``` body: ```{\n  \"error\": {\"code\":403, \"message\": \"permission denied: token missing required scope: inference.write\"}\n}```

sara (eng-runtime): couple things to check: 1) whether the token was minted as an impersonation of a service account and whether the impersonation included the inference.write scope. 2) whether their CI runner reuses tokens across jobs (race where token expired and runner retried with stale token). 3) introspect the token via our internal token-introspect endpoint to confirm scopes/aud. If they can repro, ask them to run: ```REPLY=$(curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $CI_SA_TOKEN\" https://introspect.internal.redwood/v1/token) ; echo $REPLY``` and share.

mike (platform): Also check audience claim (aud). We recently tightened accepted aud to include org-specific client_id for dedicated customers — if their pipeline gets a token with aud=ci-runner it will be rejected for certain tenants. That could show as a missing scope in our auth layer if we normalize errors.

jamie (support): customer ran introspect and returned: ```{\"active\":true, \"scope\":\"openid profile\", \"exp\":167..., \"aud\":\"ci-runner\", \"sub\":\"serviceAccount:acme-deploy-sa\"}``` so indeed the token lacks inference.write and has aud=ci-runner. they claim the ci-helper used the short-lived impersonation call: ```POST https://iam.redwood/v1/impersonate \n{\"target\":\"projects/.../serviceAccounts/acme-deploy-sa@...\", \"delegates\":[], \"scope\":[\"openid\",\"profile\"], \"lifetime\":\"300s\"}```

alex (sre): that impersonation call is the problem — the helper is not requesting our API scopes. The CI helper should include the inference.write and inference.read scopes when calling impersonate. But why did it change? did they update helper config?

sara (eng-runtime): we added a guard last month that strips non-whitelisted scopes from impersonation requests unless the requestor is platform:ci-service. If their helper recently rotated credentials and is now using a machine user without the platform role, our guard removed the inference scopes. We should check impersonation audit logs to confirm.

deploy-bot: deploy #acme-helper 2026-03-14T05:22:10Z started by acme-admin (external).

jamie (support): i attached the customer's job output showing a recent change in the helper image tag to v2.4. They rolled that out during the 03:00 UTC maintenance window. Could be tied.

mike (platform): action items: 1) sara — check impersonation audit for acme-deploy-sa between 03:00-05:00 UTC and flag any requests where scope list omitted inference.* 2) alex — confirm whether our auth layer maps aud mismatch -> missing scope error; if so, file a quick fix to surface clearer error. 3) jamie — ask customer to temporarily extend TTL to 1800s while we investigate to reduce race surface.

sara (eng-runtime): confirmed in audit: impersonate call from ci-helper service account svc-ci-helper@redwood had scope array [\"openid\",\"profile\"] at 03:11:02Z. The helper's service account lost the platform:ci-service grant during the tag rotation because infra applied a SA role tightening policy. I'll open an internal PR to re-grant and patch the helper to request inference scopes explicitly.

alex (sre): repro note for oncall: simulated a token minted without inference scopes and tried a post — got exactly the same 403 body. we probably collapse aud failures into the same code path; will adjust logging so the x-request-id surfaces aud vs scope mismatch. Patch incoming.

jamie (support): customer accepted the TTL bump and rolled back the helper tag to v2.3; pipeline green now. they want a postmortem and a recommendation for least-privilege config.

mike (platform): recommendation draft: 1) CI helper must request explicit inference.* scopes during impersonation; 2) use a signing role with well-scoped platform:ci-service principal that can't be removed by routine SA tightening; 3) set TTL to min(900s, job timeout) and add token refresh logic on retry to avoid stale tokens in queued workers; 4) add telemetry to detect tokens that lack required scopes and alert earlier.

sara (eng-runtime): i'll prepare a short playbook and a small breaking-change note for the next platform security policy rollout. includes example impersonate payload: ```{\"scope\":[\"openid\",\"profile\",\"inference.read\",\"inference.write\"], \"lifetime\":\"600s\"}``` and a CI snippet: ```export TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST https://iam.redwood/v1/impersonate -d '@payload.json' | jq -r .access_token) \ncurl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -d ...```

jamie (support): marking resolved for now, keeping thread open until sara's PR and alex's logging patch land. :thumbsup:
